I re-derived the schedule from the constraints and got the same answer. All 16 constraints hold.

Let Finn be in slot f. Elif is then in f+1, and Dev is before Finn with one person between Dev and Elif, so Dev is in f-1. Cara is two slots from Dev and can't be f+1 (Elif), so Cara is in f-3 and Ivo, directly before Cara, is in f-4. Ben is after Cara, at least three slots from Cara, and at least three slots from Elif, which forces Ben to f+4 or later. Ivo needs slot 1 or later and Ben needs slot 9 or earlier, so f = 5. That fixes Ivo 1, Cara 2, Dev 4, Finn 5, Elif 6, Ben 9. Ann must be before Finn, so Ann is in slot 3. Gus must be at least three from Ivo and Cara, and before Hana, so Gus is 7 and Hana is 8.

Checks: Ivo(1) < Finn(5); Dev(4) and Elif(6) have one person between; Ben(9) and Elif(6) are 3 apart; Cara(2) follows Ivo(1); Gus(7) and Ivo(1) are 6 apart; Ben(9) and Cara(2) are 7 apart; Ivo < Cara; Ann(3) < Finn(5); Cara(2) and Dev(4) have one person between; Cara(2) < Ben(9); Gus(7) < Hana(8); Elif(6) follows Finn(5); Ann(3) and Gus(7) are 4 apart; Ann(3) and Elif(6) are 3 apart; Cara(2) and Gus(7) are 5 apart; Dev(4) < Finn(5).

Unlike my earlier write-up, this derivation is the complete argument: the earlier phrase "Ben must be at least four slots after Cara" was loose, and the forced value of Ben comes from the Elif distance together with f = 5.

SCHEDULE: {"1":"Ivo","2":"Cara","3":"Ann","4":"Dev","5":"Finn","6":"Elif","7":"Gus","8":"Hana","9":"Ben"}
CONFIDENCE: 98
